name: Railway
tagline: Deploy apps, databases, and services with CLI and API.
shortDescription: Railway provides a CLI, GraphQL/API workflows, deployments, logs, environments, templates, and managed services.
agentSummary: Agents can deploy, inspect services, manage environment variables, and read logs through a compact CLI.
bestFor: Quick app deployment, preview-ish environments, logs, and small managed services.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Environment variables, redeploys, and deletes need review. Schema changes, migrations, deletes, backups, row-level security, and retention policies need explicit review before agents touch production data. CLI access is powerful but can run destructive local or production commands; prefer dry runs, preview environments, and non-production credentials. API automation needs client-side throttling, idempotency where supported, pagination limits, retries, and audit logging.
pricingSummary: Public usage-based pricing with free/trial credits depending on plan.
authModel: User login, account/workspace tokens, and project permissions.
browserSupport: Dashboard is useful for logs, variables, billing, and service topology.

capabilities.detail: Railway CLI supports deployment, variables, logs, linking, and service operations.
Railway exposes GraphQL/API workflows for project automation.
Docs cover CLI, deployments, variables, and public API.
Public usage-based pricing with free/trial credits depending on plan.
Dashboard is useful for logs, variables, billing, and service topology.
The tool has documented test, local, preview, self-hosted, or staging paths that let agents validate changes away from production.
